_about: Every number the manager uses. Principles: playbook/PLAYBOOK.md (the user's rules, 2026-10-09); _section names the matching section.

objective.principle: better team for less: every move leaves the XI at least as good

squad._homegrown: User, 2031-08-08: aim for at least this many homegrown (trained in England 3 years before 21) senior players. The Premier League needs 8 among 25; we had 1, so only 18 could be registered and new signings were left out. Prefer homegrown when choosing between similar targets, so we don't fill the gap with weak U21s. The export has no homegrown field: manager.homegrown approximates it (English, or joined an English club by 18 and spent 3 years there before 21).
squad._youth: Keep under-21s whose average attributes are within youth_keep_attr_gap of our first-team median; loan or sell the rest (no hidden PA).

valuation._addon_weight: Add-ons count at this fraction of face value. 1.0 (user, 2026-10-08): they are usually hit, treat them as part of the fee. Offers are judged on value = guaranteed + addon_weight x add-ons (the offer page's 'Future & Potential Total Cost with Additional Fees').

selling._overperformer: Sell high: a 26+ attacker who scored >= this many goals above his xG had a lucky season; his value peaks now and finishing regresses (a FM Moneyball YouTuber sold a 19-goals-from-12-xG striker at 27 for 46M; our own Kofane/Risser regressed the other way).
selling._loan_table: User, 2033-08-17 and 2033-09-01 (capabilities/sell/loan-table.mjs): every loan offer for our players by listed (loan list or price book) x player type (first-team = a starter in the depth chart; prospect = <= 21 or <= 23 with PA >= 160; senior = the rest). Nothing stops for the user. Obligation to buy = a sale (sell matrix); an option to buy is recorded, the loan judged by the table. Replaces youth_loan_*, listed_loan_min_wage_share and the plain-loan rule.
selling._youth_loan_starting: User, 2033-08-17 (Đukić, 20, Köln: Important Player at 50%): a youngster develops by playing; a loan that promises real minutes (these roles) is accepted at this lower wage share. Without such a promise, youth_loan_min_wage_share applies.
selling._youth_loan: Supervisor rule (2026-10-15, for the user's review): a youth player's loan offer that blocks Continue: accept if the loan pays this share of his wage or more, else reject (Adelaide 70% rejected, Wellington 80% the better offer for Sullivan).
selling._listed_loan: A first-team player we listed (surplus) loaned out with at least this share of his wage paid: accept (Backhaus at Mainz 90%, 2032-07-23). Other first-team loans stop for the user.
selling._prospects: The sell (listing) table (user, 2033-09-01; analysis/sell_table.py), summer only: surplus 22+ and every 30+ starter (cash in; the buy table replaces him) and 30+ backups/thirds on above-median wages with depth intact are listed at the role x age price; prospects (<= max_age, or <= older_max_age with PA >= older_min_pa) outside the depth chart go on the loan list; young players with PA < min_pa and surplus worth < list_min_value are let go passively: not listed, a bid accepted, contract run out (the U21s need players). Never list a player whose listing would upset him (Highly Influential): wait for bids.
selling._senior_gk: User, 2034-07-03 (Brady, 30, about to be listed as a 30+ starter): goalkeepers age differently: 33 is a keeper's 30 and they play to ~39. Every age rule (sell bands, 30+ listings, the buy table's 29+) uses the keeper's age offset (+3).
selling._sell_by_role_age: User, 2033-09-01 (Truffert, 31, free, backup on £100K/wk: Atlético's £27.5M-35M was rejected by the old matrix): the sell price is a multiple of the top of his value by his ROLE in our depth chart (analysis/depth.py, by CA, U21s counted; a player whose position falls below starter + backup + a third without him counts as a starter) and his AGE (rising <= sell_rising.max_age, prime, senior >= senior_from_age). Starters 1.5x at most (user: Didi at 1.65x = £105M was too much). Floors as before: what we paid (not for seniors), our minimum when we'd keep him.
selling._sell_rising: User, 2033-06-24: we sold too cheap. Gallardo (21, RW) went to Al-Ittihad at his value, £56M (depth 1.0x), and is valued £121.5M a year later. A player still rising (age <= max_age) sells at factor x more; a player our analysis would keep (keep: worth more to us than the market) is never sold below his minimum x min_raise_over_offer, whatever his need. Multipliers raised 2033-06-24 (core 1.3->1.5, depth 1.0->1.2, surplus 0.9->1.0): Champions League football, richer buyers. Calibration (user): FM's value follows contract length and wages (Gallardo's £121.5M is his new £370K/wk long deal), so it is a reference, not the truth; the user's estimate for Gallardo was £70-75M, i.e. ~1.3x his value then: depth 1.2 x rising 1.1 = 1.32x (£73.95M).
selling._sell_by_need: User, 2032-02-02 (Güreler, sold at £30M total, paid £17M): an unlisted player's sell price depends on how much we need him: core (a starter, or no comparable replacement) 1.3x the top of his value; depth (rotation) 1.0x; surplus (fringe) 0.9x. All prices are totals, add-ons included. Never below what we paid (x paid_floor) unless he's 30+ or in his last year. Selling a core player flags a replacement.

follow_up.Savinho: a winger such as Lennart Karl
follow_up._about: Planned buys after a sale: the autopilot stops when one of these is sold (any other depth/surplus sale carries on; a core sale always stops).

selling._late_window_days: Listed players (user, 2032-01-04, Fresneda): accept outright only at the target; counter negotiable bids from sell_ask x value down; a non-negotiable bid below the target is turned down (more bids come) until this many days before the window closes, then anything at the minimum is taken.
selling._sell_ask: User, 2031-07-22: never just reject a bid; counter at the price we'd sell for (Kislyak value £39M, bid £34M → counter £50-55M; Kayode, a player we want to keep → £95M). A player who isn't listed is for sale at sell_ask x the top of his value (above our own minimum x min_raise_over_offer); a counter or accept at that price needs no further approval. Contract in its last year: the bottom of his range. Listed players: their price book (target, then towards the minimum). Reject only once max_counters are spent.
selling._counters: Ask x v_high on the up-front fee, but at least min_raise_over_offer x their offer. Never accept a first negotiable offer.
selling._asking_price: Asking price when transfer-listing, x v_high. 1.0 when we want to sell: the top of the valuation is what a buyer will pay, and a listed player already draws lower bids (user, 2026-10-08). asking_price_deter (fm sell --deter) only for players listed but not really for sale. Answering bids is sell_ask / sell_ask_by_need, not this.
selling._price_book: fm sell (no --price) reads the live value range, records our minimum and target in local/runs/price-book.json (analysis/evaluate_offer.py --price; minimum never below minimum_vs_v_low x v_low, target never below v_high) and lists the player with asking price Unspecified (user, 2026-10-08). Bids for a player in the price book: see _late_window_days (accept at the target, counter towards it, the minimum only in the last days). Asking prices (--price, --deter) only when re-pricing an already-listed player.
selling._keep: fm sell refuses (keep him) when our minimum exceeds this x v_high: the analysis says he is worth more to us than the market pays (McKnight: range 24K-200K, replacing his output costs ~11M). --min overrides.
selling._loans: Loan offers for our players (user, 2026-10-08): with an OBLIGATION to buy, it is a sale: guaranteed = loan fee + monthly fees over the loan + obligation fee, decided like a transfer bid (price-book minimum if listed). Never reject only because it is a loan. With only an OPTION to buy (e.g. Valdimarsson: 1.8M after 25 games, optional): a plain loan, decided on wage relief and depth (escalate).
selling._listing: User 2026-10-09: anyone is for sale. Players below Highly Influential (Influential and lower) may be listed freely when the numbers say so; Highly Influential and Team Leaders at most one per window (user 2026-10-09: Influential is fine to sell) and only when really costing us (wages vs output, decline). Never sell without a replacement in the squad or an affordable target.

buying._bargains: User, 2034-08 (Rosete, Esajas, Finck: the buys we wanted that no filter found): analysis/bargains.py lists undervalued players (value <= typical/2 for their CA and age, <= 25, CA at backup level) and buried talent (<= 24, PA >= 185, CA <= 150: a big club's reserves), position-free resale buys; at most per_window buys and max_spend a window; they go on loan unless they'd start.
buying._work_permit: User, 2034-07-03: a prospect who fails his work permit is fine: he goes on the loan list until he qualifies, or is sold later with the value he gained. A rejected permit never stops for the user: appeal when the appeal costs <= work_permit_appeal_max, else don't appeal.
buying._wonderkids_buy: User, 2034-07-03: each summer buy up to wonderkids_per_window prospects with PA >= wonderkid_min_pa, aged 16-20 (18+ unless British/Irish), at most wonderkid_max_fee each, wage <= backup_max_wage; best PA first. They go on the loan list as soon as they join unless they would start. Not tied to the season surplus (an investment).
buying._table: The buy decision table (user, 2033-09-01; analysis/buy_table.py): per position from the depth chart. replace: like-for-like (CA >= his - replace_within). backup: none within backup_within of min(weakest starter, squad average of the top squad_size): the cheapest within backup_ca_spread of the best affordable (aim backup_aim_fee, max backup_max_fee, wage <= backup_max_wage); cover players count; a starter elsewhere is not a backup. upgrade (summer only): CA >= starter + upgrade_by, age <= upgrade_max_age, wage within the hard cap, paid from the season surplus (fees out - in), best CA per £ first. January: replacements and missing backups only (clubs ask more). 29+ only as free agents.
buying._max_sell_on: User, 2033-07-09: never sign a sell-on. Ortega (bought 2030 by accepting Lecce's counter) owes Lecce 40% of the profit on his next sale. fm buy removes a sell-on from a counter twice; if the club keeps it, it stops for the user instead of accepting.
buying._opening: User, 2035-06-18: Slatina, Đukić and Wark were lost to 0.85x lowballs (flat rejections, we walked; other clubs bought them); the user bid the asking price a day later and got all three. Yılmaz (final year) went for £8.5M = 0.69x value, while we paid £11.75M + £3M from the agent's range. Rules: a priority target (approval note matches priority_notes) opens at the asking price; a player in the last year of his contract opens at final_year_open_at x his profile value; after a flat rejection of a priority target, bid the asking price the next game day (local/runs/rebids.json, the autopilot places it).
buying._open_at_2033_08_05: User, 2033-08-05 ("we could have got better deals"): open at 0.85x value (0.75x when the club wants to sell), step up; a release clause is our ceiling, paid only when our offer would reach it or the club refuses.
buying._open: x FM's value (middle of the range), up-front. Was 0.9 x v_low until 2026-10-10: clubs flatly reject bids far below value (Maza, ~70M value, opened at ~45M), and a flat rejection ends the deal.
buying._raise: Each raise adds this x v_low.
buying._max: x v_high unless the analyst sets a walk-away maximum first.
buying._min_minutes_share: The export holds only ~the last 20 league games for other clubs' players (Odegaard 1800 min, Saka 1363). A target must have played this share of the minutes available in his league's window (an ever-present, the 97th-percentile player's minutes): a regular starter.
buying._personality: Scout-report traits (FM shows them as 'consistent performer' / 'enjoys big matches'): skip targets below these. GKs are judged without average rating (it mostly reflects the defence in front of them).
buying._why_a_sample_floor: Superseded by min_minutes_share. Why a floor at all: the 2027 signings were bought on ~11 apps and regressed (Kofane +3.2 G-xG, Risser +3.7 goals prevented, both flipped). Goals-minus-xG and goals prevented are mostly luck within one season.
buying._accept_loan_back: User, 2026-10-15: when the selling club asks to loan a signing back (Nürnberg for Miceli), accept: the kid plays and develops. Only for buys made to develop away: the buy approval's note matches loan_back_notes (portfolio / wonderkid / loan back). A signing bought to play now is kept (2031-07-02: Gallardo, our RW starter, was loaned back to Bayern).
buying._work_permit_appeal: A signing's work permit rejected (Lemaitre, 2030-07-18): appeal | decline | ask. User, 2026-10-15: appeal ("he's a good player"; £5K is trivial next to a signing we chose).

final_year._about: User, 2032-07-02: every final-year player through one decision matrix (capabilities/contracts/final-year.mjs): no contract -> release; 30+ and not core -> sell; replaceable (a market player aged <= replacement_max_age, role score within similar_within of his, value <= replace_value_ratio x his) -> sell and buy the replacement; worth keeping -> ask his demands (renewal preview) -> the renewal test decides renew or sell. Players worth < minor_value with < minor_minutes just run down.
final_year._max_wage_raise: User, 2032-07-02 (Savinho asked £245K-275K on £180K: too much; £220K maybe): a renewal is at most this far above his current wage; above it, list him and replace. The renewal test then counts the FULL new wage, and both paths (renew vs sell + replace) are shown.
final_year._stars: Our top-N players by CA who start are asked their demands first, even when replaceable (user: keep quality if reasonable).
final_year._quality: User, 2032-07-02: quality is FM CA (position-weighted, all attributes); a replacement is similar when his CA is within similar_ca of ours and his role score within fit_within (fit only); PA breaks ties for 23 and under.

renewal._about: User, 2026-10-15: a contracted player is a sellable asset; a final-year player is an asset losing value. Renew when the value it protects is at least min_value_x_cost x what renewing costs, even above the wage cap; else sell this window (worth sell_over+) or let him run down. Look lookahead_seasons ahead so no regular or valuable player reaches his final year undecided.
renewal.cost: (new wage - current wage) x 52 x min(years, holding_seasons) + loyalty bonus + agent fee
renewal._holding: Contract backtest (2026-10-15): renewing stops the final-year slide (-31%/-51%) but does not restore the old value, so the value is his CURRENT value; we sell within ~2 seasons, so the wage rise counts over that holding period, not the whole contract.

probe._about: User, 2026-10-15: open open_ticks under his demand (open_ticks_expensive when the demand is expensive_over+) to see his floor; his counter within firm_within_ticks of the demand = firm → offer below_counter_firm ticks under it; a bigger drop = flexible → below_counter_flexible ticks under; the last round takes his counter. Lawrence (by hand): £73K → £60K → counter £66K → £64K agreed.
probe._split: User sessions (2026-10-15): the RAISE is what is negotiated. Open at current wage + raise_share x (demand - current), then halfway between our last offer and his counter; the last round takes it. Fer López £49K→£88K demand: user £69K (= midpoint £68.5K); Lawrence £49.5K→£73K: opened £60K (midpoint £61K), counter £66K → £64K (midpoint £63.5K). Without a current wage: open_pct under the demand.
probe._open: User sessions (2026-10-15): Fresneda £87K → opened £79K (8 ticks, -9%), accepted at once; Lawrence £73K → £60K (-18%) → counter £66K → £64K. Open open_pct under the demand, at least open_min_ticks; replaces open_ticks 4/5 (too lax).

contracts._salary_ticks_down: User, 2026-10-14: take the agent's opening demand and press the Salary minus button this many times, nothing else (bonuses, clauses, length untouched); then fewer ticks, ending at the demand itself. Replaces salary_factors (typed shares of the demand).
contracts._salary_factors: Personal terms for signings: keep the agent's bonuses/clauses, offer this share of the demanded salary in turn, never above the wage cap (user rule: agents give a little on salary, are firm on the rest). Up to 1.2x since 2028-06 (Tanaka: 0.85-1.0x all got 'go away and think', and stalling made us cancel a 2.5M deal).
contracts._max_salary: Personal terms: accept a demand up to this x our FIRST-TEAM median wage (top 25 earners, analysis/wage_bands.py; ~£51K in July 2026), negotiating via salary_factors; above it, stop for a decision. The contract screen's 'Avg.' includes youth/reserves (squad median £7K) and is no longer used (user, 2026-10-08: Camara's £36-44.5K is a normal first-team wage).
contracts._wage_ceiling_2034_07_25: User, 2034-07-25 (Rosete, from Mexico, on a tiny wage): a signing's current wage is not a reference; the ceiling is what we pay our players of his CA (peers x peer_factor) and the opening is open_pct under his demand. The current-wage split stays for renewals only.
contracts._release_clause: User, 2034-06-11 (Espino, recorded): never remove a release clause (removing it raised his ask £155K→£195K/wk); set it at target_x_value x his value, down to min_x_value if needed (£61M→£80M cost +£20K/wk). A player sell-on % is fine to keep. If the wage that results is above the ceiling, walk away: Espino at £175K was accepted only as the user's exception (Fisher, our RB, earns similar). Ceiling tightened 2034-06-11: peers x 1.0, current x 2.0 (was 1.15 / 2.5: Espino came out at £155K).
contracts._wage_ceiling: User, 2033-08-05 (Ylla £180K, Espino £145K, Mokio £135K: "a bit much"): a signing's wage ceiling is the lower of (median wage of our players within peer_within_ca CA of him) x peer_factor and his current wage x current_factor. Our offers never go above it; his demand above it is negotiated down, and no agreement stops for the user. The first-team-median cap stays as the backstop.
contracts._max_salary_2033_08_05: User, 2033-06-24: in the Champions League we will pay more wages for better players. 2.5x -> 3.0x the first-team median (~£67.8K: cap £203K). Ylla (23, CA 161) asked £190K vs the old £169K cap.
contracts._max_salary_2026_10_10: User, 2026-10-10: wage is not a filter for quality signings (we buy better players now); 2.5x the first-team median (~GBP 115K) only stops runaway demands. The real limit is the club wage budget (fm offers: payrollAvailable).
contracts._negotiator: User, 2026-10-14: the manager negotiates personal terms itself with salary_ticks_down (was the Director of Football: talks were handed over).

agent_payoff._payoff: Fractions of the agent's first ask. Always settle: counter at counter_at, then accept any reply at or below accept_at_or_below (user rule, 2026-10-04).

scoreboard._about: User, 2026-10-14: the objective is net transfer profit, cumulative (not per window, so big spending that pays back is fine), within reason: wages inside a range of the budget, squad quality must not collapse, never relegated. fm audit checks these; local/runs/ledger.json holds the transfer totals.
scoreboard._release_clause: A player's minimum release clause below this x the fee we paid caps our resale profit: warn (Ortega asked £82M on a £61M fee).

autonomy_promotion._about: A capability on 'approve' is eligible for 'auto' after this many proposals in a row the user approved unchanged (fm autonomy). The user flips it in policy.autonomy.

autonomy._about: Which capabilities act on their own ('auto') and which need the user's sign-off per action and price ('approve'). Promote one to 'auto' once its tests pass consistently (user, 2026-10-14: start with buying and selling on approval).

escalate._about: Situations where the loop stops for analysis instead of a handler.
escalate._any_purchase: Superseded by autonomy (2026-10-14): buying is on approval again; this flag is not read.

holiday.return: after N days via 'Return from vacation after'; for a season: back on 05-28 (after the last league match, before the summer window)
holiday.offers: Only accept offers matching asking price
holiday._never_tick: Changed by the user 2026-10-10 for the 2028/29 season: UNTICK it, the assistant picks the XI (setting the XI is not automated). Earlier, 2026-10-09: TICK 'Use team selection where possible' so the XI we pick (new signings) plays; before, it was never ticked because forcing the XI stops rotation and risked injuries. Watch injuries in the season report; revert if they pile up.

_delegate_to_staff: Only these go to staff (Staff Responsibilities in the game). Never sales or loan offers, for any squad (user, 2026-10-18, Awudu): those come to us.

information._why: User 2026-10-09: a real manager never sees FM's CA/PA. The manager judges ability by visible attributes (1-20), stats, value, wage, age and contract.

free_agents._wonderkid_max_age: User, 2026-10-18 (Holmbjerg, PA 178, missed in January and gone to Roma): a free wonderkid (PA >= buying.table.wonderkid_min_pa, this age or younger) is always a buy: no fee. The table judges by CA/PA (PLAYBOOK §1a); foreign under-18s are not listed (they won't join).
free_agents._always_buy_max_age: User, 2032-01-01 (Truffert, 30, £100K/wk to back up Brown): the attribute-median worth flatters a 30-year-old; always-buy only up to this age. Older free agents are listed, not flagged.

free_agents._watch: Players the user picked out: always shown by the free-agent step, whatever the filters.
free_agents._about: User, 2031-05-28: free agents first. A free agent or a contract ending by 30 June (pre-contract from January; loanees count, the parent club's contract) is a buy when his worth (what the same attributes and age sell for) clears always_buy_worth: no fee, pure resale.

autopilot._watchdog: User, 2032-07-12: no new game date and no decision for this long → fm run saves a stuck report (local/runs/friction) and stops, instead of hanging.

fallback._: User, 2026-10-18: before the autopilot stops on a screen, a cheap model (claude -p, haiku) looks at it within these limits. A fact a handler can't read: the model reads only that fact, it must be on the screen, and the handler's table decides. No handler: it may press one safe_buttons button that is on the screen, or none; a screen with money_words always stops. At most max_per_run calls per run, never twice on one screen; each is logged as a supervisor-decision for review (capabilities/season/fallback.mjs).

deals._about: The deal state machine (capabilities/deals): a deal in one state longer than this (days) raises an alert; fee-agreed / contract / confirmation stuck stop the autopilot (2032-01: five agreed signings lapsed unnoticed).

first_team_bar._about: User, 2032-06-16: the assistant picks the XI, so a first-team signing only plays (develops, resells) if he is clearly better than who we have. Buy for the first team only above our current starter in the slot by role attributes (or a clear #2 for depth); a player 'about as good' sits and loses value. Prefer quality now at 21-25 (e.g. a 21-22 year old at £20M) over prospects: squad places are limited.

wonderkids._develop: User, 2026-10-19 (Slatina, 19, 148/189, and E. Đukić, 21, 164/178, were about to become ST backups): a prospect still growing (PA at least this above his CA) starts for us or plays on loan, never on our bench: he develops, then plays for us or is sold. Backups come from settled players or a cheap signing (buy table).
wonderkids._limits: User, 2026-10-18 (season-end 2036: 4 wonderkids proposed on top of the ones we hold): "we should only sign a couple... if we accumulate six new wonderkids every season and only sell one a season, that sucks". The portfolio is every prospect we own (<= 23, PA >= portfolio_min_pa, outside the depth chart, on loan or not), at most portfolio_max; a bought one needs PA >= buy_min_pa (free ones: free_agents.wonderkid_max_age, PA >= buying.table.wonderkid_min_pa) and at most buying.table.wonderkids_per_window a window. Buys only fill the room that promotions and sales leave; the sell table sells the weakest when the portfolio is over the limit.
wonderkids._cycle: User, 2034-09: bought (summer buy table: PA >= 175, 16-20, <= £15M, <= 4 a window, portfolio <= 10) → loan-listed on arrival unless he'd be a backup or starter → on loan while <= 23 and outside the depth chart (loan table) → promoted when his CA reaches our backup level (the depth chart takes him) → over 23: a normal player (surplus is sold by the sell table).
wonderkids._portfolio: At most this many prospects (23 or under, PA >= the buy table's wonderkid_min_pa, outside the depth chart) on our books at once, loaned out / U21 to develop (buy_table.py caps the summer list at the room left) (user, 2032-06-16: we can only buy so many; they don't play for us).
wonderkids._about: The wonderkid portfolio (user, 2026-10-15; again for January 2032, 2031-08-08): cheap high-potential kids, loaned out to develop and sold on. Scanned at the january checkpoint.

newgens._about: 1 May checkpoint: the new class (aged <= 16, joined since 15 Feb). Foreign under-18s are not a route (none would join, 2031-05-28); home nations can sign now.
